youtube.title: Distributed Tracing Across Generated gRPC Runtimes — Browser and Native | grpc-over-datachannels
youtube.description:
Distributed tracing (beta) for grpc-over-datachannels: register one span observer and every generated client and server — 16 native languages plus the browser — emits spans that follow the call. Nested outbound calls parent automatically, trace context propagates in the standard traceparent header, and the TCP/DataChannel proxy emits its own span, so a trace survives the hop from a stock HTTP/2 client into a DataChannel service.

Code: https://github.com/browser-grpc/grpc-over-datachannels
Release notes: https://github.com/browser-grpc/grpc-over-datachannels/releases
Blog: https://c100k.blogspot.com/2026/11/grpc-over-datachannels-0400-tracing.html

Built with Fish Audio

scenes.heading: Tracing That Follows the Call
scenes.sub: One observer. Every generated runtime. Browser and native.
scenes.say: When a call crosses three services in three languages, where did the time go? This is distributed tracing for grpc-over-datachannels: spans that follow the call through every generated runtime, in the browser and on native, with one observer to register.

scenes.heading: Why calls go dark
bullets: A request fans out across services and languages
Logs show each hop, but nothing connects them
Adding tracing by hand means plumbing context everywhere
scenes.say: A single request fans out across services, languages, and transports. Each hop logs happily, and nothing connects the logs. Hand-wiring context through every handler is exactly the kind of plumbing generated code should do for you.

scenes.heading: Register one observer
bullets: setTracer with onStart and onEnd callbacks
Spans carry kind, method, trace id, span id, parent, status, duration
Context travels in the standard traceparent header
scenes.say: Register one span observer and every generated client and server starts emitting spans: start and end events with the method, status, and duration. The context travels in the standard traceparent header, so hops that do not record still pass the trace along.

scenes.heading: Nested calls parent themselves
bullets: A handler's outbound call joins the inbound trace automatically
Explicit trace-context binding in the browser
scenes.say: The part that matters in practice: when a handler makes its own outbound call, that call joins the inbound trace with no manual plumbing. Native runtimes keep the context ambient. In the browser it binds explicitly. A client-originated call starts a root span when there is no parent.

scenes.heading: Quiet until you ask
bullets: No observer registered: nothing is recorded, nothing is sent
Unsampled contexts still propagate; they just do not record
The proxy adds its own span, so traces cross the HTTP/2 hop
scenes.say: Until an observer is registered, the runtime stays dormant: no spans, no header. Unsampled contexts still propagate end to end, they simply do not record. And the T C P to DataChannel proxy emits its own span for proxied calls, so a trace survives the hop from a stock H T T P slash two client into a DataChannel service.

scenes.heading: Checked in every language
bullets: Every language ships TRACING.md next to TESTS.md
Suites assert the full client and server parent chain
The browser matrix pairs native and WASM facade runtimes both ways
scenes.say: Every language documents tracing in its own T R A C I N G file, and the suites assert the whole chain: client span, server span, correct parent, same trace. The browser matrix pairs native and facade runtimes in both directions and checks that server spans parent to client spans, so the behaviour is proven, not just described.

scenes.heading: Live: one call, one trace, parented spans
scenes.say: Here it is live. One echo call, one trace id, and the server span parented to the client span, printed by the observer as the call happens.

scenes.heading: Try it
bullets: Designated beta, behind one central switch
scenes.say: Tracing is designated beta, behind one central switch in the generator, so it can evolve without disturbing the stable wire. If you try it, the project would like to hear where the model chafes. Links are in the description.
